data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the PKGBUILD and found it to be standard AUR packaging for a -git VCS package. The package fetches from the official GitHub repository, uses SKIP checksums (normal for VCS sources), and builds with pnpm/npx and cargo using lockfiles. No malicious code execution, data exfiltration, or suspicious patterns were detected. The inconclusive result from the first report was due to a tool error (HTTP 400 on .SRCINFO), not a security concern.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in the qwen model's audit of .SRCINFO (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), not by substantive disagreement about package safety. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. Both models agreed the PKGBUILD itself is safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .SRCINFO due to HTTP 400 error
learnings: Tool errors (HTTP 400, timeouts) should be retried or handled gracefully to avoid inconclusive verdicts on non-critical files
.SRCINFO is declarative metadata only and poses no execution risk; models should recognize this and not block verdicts on its failure
VCS packages with SKIP checksums and unpinned branches are standard AUR patterns and should not trigger false positives when the source URL points to the declared upstream repository
